grand_strategy.reading: Switzerland holds its position by being useful to everyone: venue, protecting power and financial centre to the West, tariff-deal partner to Washington, free-trade partner to Beijing. The 2026 votes (population cap and neutrality both rejected, EU package advancing) show a public that wants to keep both its market access and its neutral label, which is why Bern aligns with EU sanctions while insisting it is not aligned. The unresolved tests are the referendum on the EU package, the US tariff regime and the Patriot/F-35 dependency.

stances.note: Non-member surrounded by EU territory; the EU is partner under the ontology. Bilaterals III (signed 2 Mar 2026, 94 EU legal acts) passed the Council of States 29 to 15 on 28 Sep 2026, a popular vote is not expected before 2027 and the SVP calls it a 'treaty of submission'. Warming: the package is moving, polls (Jun 2026) show 46% for and 40% against. Bond - affinity: geography and trade (about 60% of trade), not kinship. Sanctions on Russia follow EU packages.

stances.note: Transactional, not an alliance: a 39% US tariff from 1 Aug 2025 (cut to a 15% framework on 14 Nov 2025, with a USD 200bn Swiss investment pledge to 2028) was upended by the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling on 20 Feb 2026; no final deal as of 30 Jun 2026. Swiss politicians called to cancel the F-35 over the tariff, Patriot deliveries slip four to five years with payments frozen, and the Federal Council stopped new arms-export licences to the US in March 2026 (neutrality, Iran war). Cooling for those reasons; bond - affinity (shared democratic and business ties; the US is the second-largest export market).
